title: Crown Him with Many Crowns
description: Crown Him with Many Crowns in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, five verses and a piano.
about: Matthew Bridges published Crown Him with Many Crowns in 1851. George Job Elvey, organist of St George's Chapel, Windsor, wrote the tune DIADEMATA for it in 1868; the name is Greek for 'crowns'.
underlay: Crown Him with man-y crowns, The Lamb up-on His throne; Hark! how the heav’n-ly an-them_ drowns All mu-sic but its own: A-wake, my soul, and sing Of Him who died for thee, And hail Him as thy match-less King Through all e-ter-ni-ty.

lines: Hark! how the heavenly anthem drowns
Of Him who died for thee,
And hail Him as thy matchless King
Whose arm those crimson trophies won
As of that Rose the Stem;
The Root whence mercy ever flows,
Crown Him the Lord of love!
But downward bends his burning eye
Crown Him the Lord of peace!
From pole to pole, that wars may cease,
His reign shall know no end,
Crown Him the Lord of years,
For Thou hast died for me;
Thy praise shall never, never fail
